covers: A story with a timeline and a lesson — checks the script keeps the sequence rather than jumping straight to the moral.
idea: Story about tweaking my back on a deadlift I had no business pulling, and what the comeback actually looked like: three weeks of walking and empty bar work, then starting again at a weight that felt insulting, and being back past the old number by the autumn.

hooks.rationale: Drops into the moment itself, present tense.

hooks.text: The comeback was not brave. It was insultingly light.
hooks.rationale: Contradicts what a comeback is assumed to look like.

hooks.text: You're scared of the lift that hurt you and nobody tells you what to do about that.
hooks.rationale: Names the frustration the viewer is living in.

hooks.rationale: The strongest true version, stated without hedging.

sections.text: The bar is halfway up my shins and I already know it's wrong.
I pulled a weight I had no business pulling, on a day I had decided in advance was going to be a good one.

The comeback was three weeks of walking and empty bar work, which felt like doing nothing at all. Then I started again at a weight that felt insulting, and I stayed there longer than my ego wanted to. Here's the boring part: that stretch is the comeback. The heavy day at the end is just the receipt.
By the autumn I was past the old number, and my back has not said anything about it since.
If you're in the walking and empty bar part, stay there one week longer than you want to.

voice_fidelity.evidence: The rhythm and the self-deprecation match, though "just the receipt" is a shade more writerly than the profile's plain register.

hook_distinctiveness.evidence: Four separate promises, but the cold open and the pain hook both trade on the same fear.

script_completeness.evidence: Sequence is intact, the body pays off the hook, and the ask is one specific week.

instruction_adherence.evidence: The timeline is the creator's own and no rehab protocol, clinician or study is invented around it.
